1	# Nope-Mode — Design Specification
     2	
     3	Android app for GrapheneOS. Selected apps go silent and un-openable, on a
     4	schedule or on demand.
     5	
     6	A cleanroom equivalent of Google's Focus Mode, which does not exist on
     7	GrapheneOS because Digital Wellbeing is not shipped and cannot be installed
     8	from Play.
     9	
    10	**Status:** WS1 and WS4 landed. WS2, WS3, WS5–WS11 unbuilt.
    11	**Target:** Pixel 9 Pro (`caiman`), GrapheneOS, Android 17 / SDK 37.
    12	**Provisioned:** device owner is live on the target device as of 2026-08-03.
    13	
    14	---
    15	
    16	## 1. Cleanroom provenance
    17	
    18	This repository is **all rights reserved**. Every close prior art is
    19	**GPL-3.0**. Copying from them would force this project to GPL.
    20	
    21	**What was studied:** F-Droid listings, README files, published feature
    22	descriptions, user-facing behavior, and official Android API documentation.
    23	
    24	**What was never opened:** the source code of Hail, NotiFilter, DetoxDroid,
    25	Curbox Detox, or Open TimeLimit.
    26	
    27	Behavioral *ideas* are not copyrightable; expression is. What follows is
    28	derived from documented behavior and the public Android SDK. Anyone extending
    29	this project must hold the same line: **read their docs, never their source.**
    30	
    31	### Prior art and what each contributed
    32	
    33	| Project | License | What was taken (behavior only) |
    34	|---|---|---|
    35	| Google Focus Mode | proprietary | The target behavior itself: pick distracting apps, pause them, schedule it, and offer a **bounded** "take a break" (5/15/30 min). Grayed-out icons as the paused signal. |
    36	| [Hail](https://github.com/aistra0528/Hail) | GPL-3.0 | Confirmation that suspend-based freezing is the right mechanism, and that disable/hide/suspend are meaningfully different. |
    37	| [NotiFilter](https://github.com/BURG3R5/NotiFilter) | GPL-3.0 | That notification-listener filtering is viable as a fallback, and that scheduling windows belong on the filter itself. |
    38	| [DetoxDroid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.flx_apps.digitaldetox/) | GPL-3.0 | **"Protection always on"** — you pause deliberately, it auto-resumes, and there is a *minimum interval between pauses*. This is the single most important behavioral idea in the whole design (§9). |
    39	| [Curbox Detox](https://f-droid.org/packages/neth.iecal.curbox/) | FOSS | Graduated bypass resistance: strict / timed / per-attempt / challenge / capped attempt counts. |
    40	
    41	---
    42	
    43	## 2. Requirements
    44	
    45	**R1.** Maintain a user-selected list of blocked apps.
    46	**R2.** When active, blocked apps emit no notification, no sound, no vibration.
    47	**R3.** When active, blocked apps cannot be opened.
    48	**R4.** Activate manually, from a quick-settings tile, or on a schedule.
    49	**R5.** Ship with a default schedule of **20:00 → 08:00, every day**, enabled.
    50	**R6.** Deactivating restores every app to exactly its prior state.
    51	**R7.** Survive reboots, including a reboot in the middle of a window.
    52	**R8.** Never silently under-enforce. If a block fails, say so.
    53	**R9.** While active, the phone must not ring except for **starred contacts**,
    54	plus **repeat callers** when that toggle is on. See §18.
    55	
    56	### Non-goals
    57	
    58	- Usage analytics, screen-time charts, streaks, leaderboards.
    59	- Per-app time budgets. Nope-Mode is binary: blocked or not.
    60	- Website or URL blocking, keyword filtering of notification content.
    61	- Grayscale, doomscroll detection, Extra Dim. (DetoxDroid does these; they are
    62	  a different product.)
    63	- Parental controls, remote administration, accounts, telemetry.
    64	- **Any network access whatsoever.** The app declares no `INTERNET` permission
    65	  and must never gain one.
    66	
    67	---
    68	
    69	## 3. Decisions
    70	
    71	| # | Decision | Rationale |
    72	|---|---|---|
    73	| D1 | **Device owner is the primary enforcement mechanism** | `setPackagesSuspended` is the only no-root API delivering R2 *and* R3, and it survives reboots (R7). Shizuku was rejected: it must be re-armed after every reboot, silently breaking an unattended overnight schedule — precisely the failure the app exists to prevent. |
    74	| D2 | **Notification listener + accessibility is the fallback tier** | Zero provisioning, works anywhere. Strictly weaker (§8.2) but the app is never useless. |
    75	| D3 | **Blocked apps are un-openable, not merely silent** | Full Focus Mode parity. Suspension delivers R2 and R3 in one call, so this costs nothing extra. |
    76	| D4 | **Kotlin + Views, no Compose** | Matches PiercingXX-Launcher exactly. |
    77	| D5 | **Public repo, all rights reserved** | Matches the launcher. Consequence: cleanroom discipline per §1, permanently. |
    78	| D6 | **Room + Gson** | Same stack as the launcher, so backup JSON conventions carry over. |
    79	| D7 | **Breaks are always time-bounded** | An unbounded "off" turns a schedule into a suggestion. See §9. |
    80	| D8 | **State is derived, never accumulated** | A pure function of (now, schedules, override). Makes missed or duplicated alarms harmless. See §6. |
    81	
    82	### 3.1 Device owner — the standing cost
    83	
    84	Device owner is a full MDM role, and this is a real tradeoff, not a formality:
    85	
    86	- Settings will report the device as managed.
    87	- **Some apps refuse to run on managed devices** — banking, certain DRM video.
    88	- The user cannot remove it through Settings. Nope-Mode **must** expose
    89	  *Relinquish device owner* → `clearDeviceOwnerApp()`. Without it the only exit
    90	  is a factory reset. Implemented in WS4; do not remove it.
    91	- Only one device owner may exist. Nope-Mode holds that slot for the life of
    92	  the install.
    93	
    94	### 3.2 Provisioning window (historical, now satisfied)
    95	
    96	Device owner can only be set on a device with **zero accounts**:
    97	
    98	```sh
    99	adb shell dpm set-device-owner \
   100	    com.piercingxx.nopemode/.admin.NopeDeviceAdminReceiver
   101	```
   102	
   103	This was provisioned on 2026-08-03 after a factory reset. **It cost one wipe to
   104	learn that opening the Google apps first closes the window.** If device owner is
   105	ever relinquished, regaining it costs another full reset — treat it as
   106	non-renewable.
   107	
   108	---
   109	
   110	## 4. Platform mechanics
   111	
   112	Authoritative behavior of `DevicePolicyManager.setPackagesSuspended`, from
   113	Android documentation. The whole design rests on this, so it is quoted rather
   114	than paraphrased loosely.
   115	
   116	A suspended package:
   117	
   118	- cannot start activities;
   119	- has its **notifications hidden**;
   120	- does **not** appear in the recents / overview screen;
   121	- cannot show toasts, dialogs, or snackbars;
   122	- **cannot play audio or vibrate the device**;
   123	- shows a system "app is paused" dialog when tapped;
   124	- is **grayed out in the launcher**.
   125	
   126	That single call satisfies R2 and R3 completely. No notification listener, no
   127	accessibility service, no DND manipulation is required at this tier.
   128	
   129	### 4.1 Packages that cannot be suspended
   130	
   131	The platform refuses these outright. The picker must exclude them at
   132	**selection time**, not fail at enforcement time:
   133	
   134	- Device admins — **this includes Nope-Mode itself**
   135	- The **active launcher** (suspending it bricks the home screen)
   136	- The required **package installer**, **uninstaller**, and **verifier**
   137	- The **default dialer**
   138	- The **permission controller**
   139	
   140	Two more that the platform *permits* but which must be guarded anyway:
   141	
   142	- **The active input method.** Suspending the keyboard leaves the user unable
   143	  to type — including unable to type their way out. Hard-block it.
   144	- **The default SMS handler.** Permitted, and a legitimate choice for some, but
   145	  it silences 2FA codes. Require an explicit confirmation; never reachable via
   146	  bulk-select.
   147	
   148	`setPackagesSuspended` **returns the array of packages it could not suspend.**
   149	Never discard it (R8).
   150	
   151	---
   152	
   153	## 5. Architecture
   154	
   155	```
   156	        ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
   157	        │           NopeController           │  owns desired state
   158	        │  derive(now, schedules, override)  │  talks to no Android API
   159	        └──────────────────┬─────────────────┘
   160	                           │ desired: Set<packageName>
   161	        ┌──────────────────▼─────────────────┐
   162	        │         Enforcer (interface)       │
   163	        └────────┬──────────────────┬────────┘
   164	                 │                  │
   165	      ┌──────────▼──────┐   ┌───────▼─────────────────┐
   166	      │ SuspendEnforcer │   │    FallbackEnforcer     │
   167	      │  device owner   │   │  listener + a11y        │
   168	      └─────────────────┘   └─────────────────────────┘
   169	```
   170	
   171	`NopeController` computes *what should be true* and hands it to an `Enforcer`.
   172	It imports nothing from `android.*`. That is what makes the scheduling logic —
   173	the part that must be correct — testable on the JVM with no device.
   174	
   175	Tier selection, re-evaluated whenever admin state changes:
   176	
   177	```
   178	if (dpm.isDeviceOwnerApp(packageName)) SuspendEnforcer else FallbackEnforcer
   179	```
   180	
   181	The active tier must be **visible in the UI at all times**. A user on the
   182	fallback tier is getting weaker protection and has to know it (R8).
   183	
   184	---
   185	
   186	## 6. State model
   187	
   188	The heart of the app. Everything else is plumbing.
   189	
   190	```kotlin
   191	sealed interface Override {
   192	    data object None : Override
   193	    data class ForceOn(val until: Instant?) : Override   // null = indefinite
   194	    data class Break(val until: Instant) : Override      // ALWAYS bounded
   195	}
   196	
   197	fun isActive(now, schedules, override): Boolean = when (override) {
   198	    is Override.ForceOn -> override.until == null || now < override.until
   199	    is Override.Break   -> if (now < override.until) false
   200	                           else scheduleSaysActive(now, schedules)
   201	    Override.None       -> scheduleSaysActive(now, schedules)
   202	}
   203	```
   204	
   205	| Override | Schedule | Result |
   206	|---|---|---|
   207	| `None` | inactive | inactive |
   208	| `None` | active | **active** |
   209	| `ForceOn(null)` | either | **active**, indefinitely |
   210	| `ForceOn(t)`, now < t | either | **active** |
   211	| `ForceOn(t)`, now ≥ t | — | expires → re-derive from schedule |
   212	| `Break(t)`, now < t | active | inactive (break running) |
   213	| `Break(t)`, now ≥ t | active | **active** — break expired, auto-resume |
   214	
   215	**`Break` has no unbounded variant, by construction.** There is no way to
   216	express "off until I say so". This is D7, and it is the difference between a
   217	schedule and a suggestion.
   218	
   219	---
   220	
   221	## 7. Scheduling
   222	
   223	```kotlin
   224	data class Schedule(
   225	    val id: Long,
   226	    val startMinuteOfDay: Int,   // 20:00 -> 1200
   227	    val endMinuteOfDay: Int,     // 08:00 -> 480
   228	    val daysMask: Int,           // bit 0 = Monday .. bit 6 = Sunday
   229	    val enabled: Boolean,
   230	)
   231	```
   232	
   233	**Windows cross midnight.** `end <= start` means the window wraps into the next
   234	day. The shipped default (1200 → 480) does exactly this, so **the wrap is the
   235	common path, not an edge case.** Test it first, before the non-wrapping case.
   236	
   237	`daysMask` refers to the day the window **starts**. A Friday-enabled 20:00→08:00
   238	window runs Friday 20:00 through Saturday 08:00. A user unchecking Saturday
   239	expects Saturday *night* to be unblocked, not Saturday *morning* — say so in the
   240	UI, because both readings are defensible.
   241	
   242	### 7.1 Reconciliation, not event-chasing
   243	
   244	```kotlin
   245	fun shouldBeActiveAt(now: LocalDateTime, schedules: List<Schedule>): Boolean
   246	```
   247	
   248	Pure. State is **always** obtained by calling this, never by accumulating alarm
   249	events (D8). Alarms merely prompt re-evaluation. A missed, late, or duplicated
   250	alarm therefore cannot corrupt state — the system is self-healing.
   251	
   252	`reconcile()` runs on: boot completed, alarm fired, app foregrounded, tile
   253	clicked, schedule edited, blocked-list edited, break started or expired,
   254	`TIME_SET`, `TIMEZONE_CHANGED`.
   255	
   256	### 7.2 Alarms
   257	
   258	- `setExactAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP, …)` for **the next boundary only**;
   259	  recompute and re-arm after each fire. Never pre-schedule a chain.
   260	- `USE_EXACT_ALARM` (API 33+), plus `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` for the minSdk 24
   261	  range. If `canScheduleExactAlarms()` is false, degrade to
   262	  `setAndAllowWhileIdle` **and show a persistent warning** — an inexact 20:00
   263	  boundary can drift by minutes, which is visible and wrong.
   264	- `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` → re-arm and reconcile. Without this the schedule
   265	  dies at the first reboot, which is exactly the Shizuku failure D1 rejected.
   266	
   267	---
   268	
   269	## 8. Enforcement tiers
   270	
   271	### 8.1 SuspendEnforcer — primary
   272	
   273	```kotlin
   274	dpm.setPackagesSuspended(admin, packages, true)   // engage
   275	dpm.setPackagesSuspended(admin, packages, false)  // release
   276	```
   277	
   278	Order of operations matters for crash safety:
   279	
   280	1. Write intended packages to `suspend_record`.
   281	2. Call `setPackagesSuspended(…, true)`.
   282	3. Inspect the returned failure array; record and surface any failures.
   283	
   284	Releasing reverses it: suspend-false first, then clear `suspend_record` only
   285	for packages that actually released.
   286	
   287	If the process dies between (1) and (2), reconcile-on-boot sees a record with
   288	nothing suspended and re-derives — harmless. If it dies between (2) and (3),
   289	the record is authoritative and the apps get released correctly. **Writing the
   290	record first is what makes a crash recoverable rather than stranding apps.**
   291	
   292	### 8.2 FallbackEnforcer — no device owner
   293	
   294	**a) `NopeNotificationListener : NotificationListenerService`**
   295	On `onNotificationPosted`, if the package is blocked and the mode is active,
   296	`cancelNotification(sbn.key)`; prefer `snoozeNotification(key, duration)` where
   297	it fits, since it suppresses re-post without a visible dismissal.
   298	
   299	> **Stated limitation, which must appear in the UI verbatim in spirit:** the
   300	> notification has already been posted when the listener sees it, so **the alert
   301	> sound may play before suppression**. This tier delivers "the notification goes
   302	> away", not "the notification never made a sound". It does not satisfy R2.
   303	
   304	**b) `NopeAccessibilityService : AccessibilityService`**
   305	On `TYPE_WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED`, read the foreground package; if blocked and
   306	active, launch `BlockedActivity` with `FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK`. Debounce to
   307	avoid launch loops.
   308	
   309	Do **not** use `performGlobalAction(GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK)` as the block — it
   310	fights the user's navigation and behaves inconsistently across launchers.
   311	
   312	---
   313	
   314	## 9. Breaks and anti-bypass
   315	
   316	Adopted from DetoxDroid's "protection always on" and Curbox's graduated
   317	resistance. Without this, a schedule is decoration — at 2am the user simply
   318	turns it off.
   319	
   320	**Baseline (ship in WS7):**
   321	
   322	- **Take a break** offers **5 / 15 / 30 minutes**, matching Focus Mode. No
   323	  custom-duration field, no "until I turn it back on".
   324	- Breaks **auto-resume**. There is no user action required to re-engage.
   325	- A break shows a persistent countdown notification from Nope-Mode itself, so
   326	  it is never ambiguous whether protection is on.
   327	
   328	**Friction (WS7, configurable, default on):**
   329	
   330	- **Minimum interval between breaks** — default 30 minutes. Prevents chaining
   331	  5-minute breaks into an unbounded evening.
   332	- **Break budget** — default 3 per active window. Exhausted means exhausted.
   333	
   334	**Deferred, explicitly out of scope for v1:**
   335	
   336	- Typing a sentence, scanning a QR code, or a commitment password. These are
   337	  proven patterns (Curbox, DetoxDroid) but they are anti-features until the
   338	  basics are solid. Revisit only if the baseline proves too easy to defeat.
   339	
   340	Every friction setting must be **editable only while Nope-Mode is inactive.**
   341	Otherwise the 2am workaround is simply to raise the break budget.
   342	
   343	---
   344	
   345	## 10. Data model (Room)
   346	
   347	```
   348	blocked_app      packageName TEXT PK, addedAt INTEGER
   349	schedule         id INTEGER PK, startMinuteOfDay INT, endMinuteOfDay INT,
   350	                 daysMask INT, enabled INT
   351	app_state        id INTEGER PK (=1), overrideKind TEXT, overrideUntil INTEGER NULL,
   352	                 lastReconcileAt INTEGER
   353	suspend_record   packageName TEXT PK, suspendedAt INTEGER
   354	break_log        id INTEGER PK, startedAt INTEGER, durationMinutes INT
   355	```
   356	
   357	- `suspend_record` — crash safety net (§8.1). On boot, anything present here
   358	  but no longer scheduled to be blocked is released. Without this table a crash
   359	  mid-activation can leave apps permanently suspended with no UI to recover them.
   360	- `break_log` — enforces minimum interval and break budget (§9).
   361	
   362	Seed migration inserts the default schedule `(1200, 480, all days, enabled)`.
   363	
   364	---
   365	
   366	## 11. UI
   367	
   368	Five screens. Views + viewBinding, AMOLED-black monochrome, matching the
   369	launcher.
   370	
   371	1. **Home** — large active/inactive state; the *reason* ("scheduled until
   372	   08:00", "break, 12 min left"); master toggle; **Take a break** button when
   373	   active; blocked-app count; **enforcement-tier badge**.
   374	2. **Blocked apps** — searchable list of launchable packages with icons and
   375	   checkboxes. Packages from §4.1 shown disabled **with the reason inline** —
   376	   not silently absent, or the user assumes it's blocked when it isn't.
   377	3. **Schedules** — list, add, edit, delete. Time pickers plus day-of-week
   378	   selector. Default row pre-seeded. Show the wrap explicitly: *"20:00 tonight
   379	   → 08:00 tomorrow"*.
   380	4. **Settings** — break duration options, minimum interval, break budget.
   381	   **Locked while active** (§9).
   382	5. **Setup / status** — tier, provisioning command, fallback permission grants,
   383	   and **Relinquish device owner** with a plain-language warning.
   384	
   385	`BlockedActivity` — the fallback tier's full-screen interstitial. One word,
   386	*Nope.*, the app name, and when the block lifts.
   387	
   388	### 11.1 Quick Settings tile
   389	
   390	`NopeTileService : TileService` — toggles `ForceOn` / clears it. Label and state
   391	must track derived state even when changed elsewhere
   392	(`requestListeningState`).
   393	
   394	On the target device this tile replaces the dead Digital Wellbeing Focus Mode
   395	tile, which cannot work on GrapheneOS. Note the shade layout **cannot be set
   396	programmatically on Android 17** — `sysui_qs_tiles` is vestigial and the real
   397	storage is root-only — so tile placement is always a manual user step. Do not
   398	waste effort automating it.
   399	
   400	---
   401	
   402	## 12. Manifest
   403	
   404	```xml
   405	<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED"/>
   406	<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_EXACT_ALARM"/>
   407	<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM"/>
   408	<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES"/>
   409	<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"/>
   410	<!-- deliberately NO android.permission.INTERNET -->
   411	```
   412	
   413	Components: `NopeDeviceAdminReceiver` (+ `res/xml/device_admin.xml`),
   414	`NopeNotificationListener`, `NopeAccessibilityService`, `NopeTileService`,
   415	`BootReceiver` (`BOOT_COMPLETED`, `TIME_SET`, `TIMEZONE_CHANGED`).
   416	
   417	`POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is for Nope-Mode's own break countdown only.
   418	
   419	The absent `INTERNET` permission is a verifiable privacy claim. Keep it true;
   420	it is checkable with `aapt2 dump permissions`.
   421	
   422	---
   423	
   424	## 13. Package layout
   425	
   426	```
   427	com.piercingxx.nopemode
   428	├── admin/      NopeDeviceAdminReceiver, DeviceOwnerManager          [WS4 done]
   429	├── core/       NopeController, ScheduleEvaluator, Override, BreakPolicy
   430	├── enforce/    Enforcer, SuspendEnforcer, FallbackEnforcer
   431	├── data/       entities, DAOs, NopeDatabase, BackupJson
   432	├── schedule/   AlarmScheduler, BootReceiver
   433	├── service/    NopeNotificationListener, NopeAccessibilityService,
   434	│               NopeTileService
   435	└── ui/         HomeActivity, BlockedAppsActivity, SchedulesActivity,
   436	                SettingsActivity, SetupActivity, BlockedActivity
   437	```
   438	
   439	---
   440	
   441	## 14. Failure modes
   442	
   443	| Scenario | Required behaviour |
   444	|---|---|
   445	| Crash while apps suspended | `suspend_record` + boot reconcile releases them |
   446	| Reboot mid-window | `BootReceiver` reconciles; apps re-suspend |
   447	| Exact alarm permission denied | Degrade to inexact, warn persistently, keep reconciling |
   448	| User selects own launcher / IME | Blocked at selection time with an inline reason |
   449	| `setPackagesSuspended` returns failures | Name the apps that failed; never report success (R8) |
   450	| Device owner relinquished while active | Release everything **first**, then drop to fallback |
   451	| Blocked app uninstalled | Prune from `blocked_app` and `suspend_record` on reconcile |
   452	| Schedule edited mid-window | Reconcile immediately; may deactivate instantly |
   453	| DST shift inside a window | Compare minute-of-day on local time; test the 02:00 jump |
   454	| Break spans the window end | Break expires, schedule already over → stays inactive |
   455	| Clock moved backwards | `Break.until` in the future by more than max duration → cancel the break |
   456	
   457	---
   458	
   459	## 15. Testing
   460	
   461	`ScheduleEvaluator` and the override model are pure JVM by design. They carry
   462	the weight.
   463	
   464	- `shouldBeActiveAt`: normal window; **midnight-crossing window (the default)**;
   465	  exact boundary minutes 20:00:00 and 08:00:00; day-mask boundaries across the
   466	  wrap; DST spring-forward and fall-back inside a window.
   467	- Full override truth table (§6), including `ForceOn` and `Break` expiry, and
   468	  the clock-moved-backwards guard.
   469	- `BreakPolicy`: minimum interval, budget exhaustion, budget reset at window end.
   470	- Backup JSON round-trip.
   471	- Instrumented: Room migrations; `suspend_record` recovery after a simulated
   472	  crash; a real suspend/release cycle on-device.
   473	
   474	**A workstream with failing tests is not done.**
   475	
   476	---
   477	
   478	## 16. Build
   479	
   480	```
…[125 lines NOT shown — 480/613 read. Last lines of the file follow so you can see where it ends; they are NOT contiguous with the block above.]…

   609	  a genuine emergency is worse than one unwanted ring. The user can turn it off.

   488	`applicationId` / `namespace`: `com.piercingxx.nopemode`. Debug keystore shared

   492	> launcher) but means three API levels of untested drift. Verify

   495	
   496	---
   497	
   498	## 17. Build order
   499	
   500	| WS | Scope | State |
   501	|---|---|---|
   502	| 1 | Skeleton — gradle, manifest, packages, icon | **done** |
   503	| 4 | Device admin receiver, `DeviceOwnerManager`, relinquish | **done, provisioned** |
   504	| 2 | Room entities, DAOs, seed migration | next |
   505	| 3 | `ScheduleEvaluator`, `Override`, `BreakPolicy` — pure JVM, fully tested | next |
   506	| 5 | `SuspendEnforcer`, `suspend_record`, failure surfacing | |
   507	| 6 | `AlarmScheduler`, `BootReceiver`, reconcile-on-everything | |
   508	| 7 | UI, five screens, break friction | |
   509	| 8 | QS tile | |
   510	| 9 | `FallbackEnforcer` — listener + accessibility | |
   511	| 10 | Gson backup/restore | |
   512	
   513	WS1–6 produce a fully functional headless app. UI is deliberately late: the
   514	scheduling logic is the part that has to be right, and it is the part that can
   515	be proven correct without a device.
   516	
   517	WS3 is the highest-risk workstream and has no Android dependencies — build it
   518	against tests first, in isolation.
   519	
   520	---
   521	
   522	## 18. Ringer policy — "Quiet Ringer" (R9)
   523	
   524	App suspension cannot silence the phone. The dialer is one of the packages the
   525	platform refuses to suspend (§4.1), and correctly so. Calls therefore need a
   526	second, independent mechanism.
   527	
   528	### 18.1 Scope — why this is calls-only
   529	
   530	DND cannot be scoped to a set of apps. `ZenPolicy` is a **global** interruption
   531	filter with category-level exceptions; there is no API to apply it to five
   532	chosen packages.
   533	
   534	That is fine, because **the blocked-app list already silences the apps it
   535	covers** — a suspended app cannot post a notification, play audio, or vibrate
   536	(§4). Nothing about the ringer is needed to achieve that.
   537	
   538	So the division of labour is:
   539	
   540	| Concern | Mechanism | Scope |
   541	|---|---|---|
   542	| Selected apps go silent and un-openable | `setPackagesSuspended` | the checkbox list |
   543	| Phone must not ring | `AutomaticZenRule` | the ringer, which is global by nature |
   544	
   545	The zen rule **must not** be used to silence app notifications generally. Doing
   546	so would quiet apps the user never selected, breaking the app's central promise
   547	that it only touches what you picked.
   548	
   549	### 18.2 Mechanism
   550	
   551	`AutomaticZenRule` (API 24+), owned by Nope-Mode, with a `ZenPolicy` that
   552	overrides global policy only while the rule is active.
   553	
   554	```
   555	permission : android.permission.ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY
   556	             (user grant: Settings → Do Not Disturb access)
   557	
   558	create once : NotificationManager.addAutomaticZenRule(rule) -> id, persisted
   559	activate    : setAutomaticZenRuleState(id, Condition.STATE_TRUE)
   560	deactivate  : setAutomaticZenRuleState(id, Condition.STATE_FALSE)
   561	```
   562	
   563	`ZenPolicy`:
   564	
   565	- **Calls:** allowed from **starred contacts only**.
   566	- **Repeat callers:** allowed iff the user toggle is on. This is a built-in
   567	  DND category, not something Nope-Mode implements — a second call from the
   568	  same number inside the platform's window rings through.
   569	- Everything else in the policy is left at its default. The rule exists to
   570	  restrict the ringer, not to become a general notification filter (§18.1).
   571	
   572	Rule state is driven by the **same derived `isActive`** as everything else
   573	(§6). It is set inside `reconcile()`; there is no separate scheduler.
   574	
   575	### 18.3 Why starred contacts rather than an in-app list
   576	
   577	`CallScreeningService` + `ROLE_CALL_SCREENING` would allow an arbitrary
   578	per-number whitelist, and was rejected:
   579	
   580	- It is bound **before the device rings** and must respond within **5 seconds**
   581	  or the platform times out — a slow or crashed lookup delays or drops a real
   582	  call.
   583	- Only one app can hold the role, so it would collide with any spam-blocking
   584	  app.
   585	- Repeat-caller logic would become ours to write and test, instead of being a
   586	  platform guarantee.
   587	
   588	Starred contacts is a whitelist that already exists, is edited in Contacts, is
   589	a single source of truth across the whole system, and cannot make the phone
   590	fail to ring because of a bug in this app. Revisit only if starring proves too
   591	coarse in real use.
   592	
   593	### 18.4 Failure modes
   594	
   595	| Scenario | Required behaviour |
   596	|---|---|
   597	| `ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY` not granted | Ringer policy is inert. **Say so loudly on Home** — a silently non-functional Quiet Ringer is the worst outcome here (R8). Never show "active" while the ringer is unrestricted. |
   598	| App crashes while rule is active | Rule state is re-derived on boot and on foreground; reconcile sets it false when inactive. |
   599	| App uninstalled while rule is active | `removeAutomaticZenRule` on teardown. A stranded rule would leave the phone permanently quiet with the owning app gone. |
   600	| Device owner relinquished | Unrelated — the zen rule does not depend on device owner and keeps working. |
   601	| User has manual DND on independently | Nope-Mode owns *its* rule only; it must never write global DND state or fight the user's own setting. |
   602	| No starred contacts exist | Valid, and means nothing rings. Warn once at setup — it is a plausible mistake, not necessarily an intent. |
   603	
   604	### 18.5 Settings
   605	
   606	- **Quiet Ringer** — master on/off for the whole feature. Default **on**.
   607	- **Allow repeat callers** — default **on**. A second call from the same number
   608	  is the closest thing to an emergency signal the platform offers, and missing
   609	  a genuine emergency is worse than one unwanted ring. The user can turn it off.
   610	
   611	Both live in the Settings screen and, like the break-friction settings, are
   612	**editable only while Nope-Mode is inactive** (§9).

     8	/**
     9	 * Which enforcement tier is available, and the one action that gives it up.
    10	 *
    11	 * Nope-Mode has two tiers (design.md §4). [Tier.DEVICE_OWNER] can suspend
    12	 * packages outright; [Tier.FALLBACK] can only cancel notifications after
    13	 * they have already posted, so a sound may escape first. Callers must be able
    14	 * to tell the user which one they are actually on — silently degrading would
    15	 * make the app claim protection it isn't providing.
    16	 */
    17	class DeviceOwnerManager(context: Context) {
    18	
    19	    private val appContext = context.applicationContext
    20	    private val dpm =
    21	        appContext.getSystemService(Context.DEVICE_POLICY_SERVICE) as DevicePolicyManager
    22	
    23	    enum class Tier { DEVICE_OWNER, FALLBACK }
    24	
    25	    val adminComponent: ComponentName
    26	        get() = NopeDeviceAdminReceiver.componentName(appContext)
    27	
    28	    fun isDeviceOwner(): Boolean =
    29	        dpm.isDeviceOwnerApp(appContext.packageName)
    30	
    31	    fun tier(): Tier =
    32	        if (isDeviceOwner()) Tier.DEVICE_OWNER else Tier.FALLBACK
    33	
    34	    /**
    35	     * The exact command to run over ADB to provision. Surfaced in the setup
    36	     * screen because it can only be run on a device with zero accounts — once
    37	     * an account exists the window is closed and reopening it costs a factory
    38	     * reset.
    39	     */
    40	    fun provisioningCommand(): String =
    41	        "adb shell dpm set-device-owner ${appContext.packageName}/" +
    42	            ".admin.NopeDeviceAdminReceiver"
    43	
    44	    /**
    45	     * Give up device owner. Without this the only way off the MDM role is a
    46	     * factory reset, so it is a hard requirement rather than a convenience
    47	     * (design.md §2.2).
    48	     *
    49	     * Callers MUST release every suspended package first — once this returns,
    50	     * [DevicePolicyManager.setPackagesSuspended] is no longer callable and
    51	     * anything still suspended is stranded.
    52	     *
    53	     * @return true if device owner was relinquished.
    54	     */
    55	    fun relinquish(): Boolean {
    56	        if (!isDeviceOwner()) return false
    57	        return try {
    58	            dpm.clearDeviceOwnerApp(appContext.packageName)
    59	            Log.i(TAG, "device owner relinquished")
    60	            true
    61	        } catch (e: SecurityException) {
    62	            Log.e(TAG, "failed to relinquish device owner", e)
    63	            false
    64	        }
    65	    }

    69	    }

computation is T4 (buildable); the AlarmManager/BroadcastReceiver wiring is not.

boot.

durations 5/15/30, min interval, budget — locked while active), Setup (tier,

interstitial, break countdown notification, AMOLED-black monochrome. **Verify
on-device:** every state in design §6 is reachable and legible from the UI.

tile reflects state changed from the app, and vice versa. Tile *placement* in
the shade stays a manual user step (`sysui_qs_tiles` is vestigial on Android 17).

`NopeNotificationListener` (cancel/snooze blocked packages while active),
`NopeAccessibilityService` (foreground detection → `BlockedActivity`), debounce
against launch loops, and UI stating plainly that this tier can let a sound
through and therefore does not satisfy R2. **Verify on-device:** with device
owner relinquished, blocks still work at the weaker tier.

a loud Home warning when not granted, `removeAutomaticZenRule` on teardown, never
writing global DND state, and a one-time warning when the user has no starred
contacts. **Verify on-device:** with Nope-Mode active, a call from a non-starred
number does not ring; a starred contact does; toggling repeat callers changes
second-call behaviour; revoking DND access surfaces a visible warning. The zen
rule governs **the ringer only** — never app notifications generally (design
§18.1).

---

Signed — Skippy, 2026-

## Rules for this marathon

Honored verbatim from todo.md's cross-cutting rules, plus the toolchain law:

- **Cleanroom only.** Hail, NotiFilter, DetoxDroid, and Curbox are GPL-3.0 or
  otherwise foreign-licensed; this repo is all-rights-reserved. **Read their
  docs, never their source** (design §1).
- **No `INTERNET` permission**, ever — a verifiable claim, checkable with
  `aapt2 dump permissions`.
- Tests gate each workstream. Failing tests means not done.
- **Never report success for a package the platform refused to suspend** (R8).
- Friction settings are editable only while Nope-Mode is inactive, or the 2am
  workaround is simply to raise the break budget.

Toolchain law (this machine):

- A verify **runs behavior** — a named gradle unit-test class via
  `testDebugUnitTest --tests '…'`. It never greps, never reads a file to
  "prove" behavior.
- **No two tasks share a verify command.** Each `- verify:` is a distinct
  `--tests` target.
- **No task's verify equals the final gate.** The full
  `assembleDebug testDebugUnitTest` is reserved for the marathon's final gate.
- Every added code path gets wiring proven by test where a JVM test can prove
  it. Code whose behavior only a device can prove is **deferred**, not faked
  with a weaker check.
- There is **no emulator and no device** on this machine. Instrumented tests
  (`androidTest`) and every on-device gate are operator work. Never substitute a
  weaker check and claim it proves device behavior.
- The tested layer must carry **zero `android.*` imports** (design §3/§5/§15) —
  that is what makes the scheduling logic JVM-provable.

## Buildable tasks

### T1 — ScheduleEvaluator: `shouldBeActiveAt` with midnight-crossing windows

`ScheduleEvaluator.shouldBeActiveAt(now: LocalDateTime, schedules: List<Schedule>): Boolean`
— pure, no `android.*`. Windows where `end <= start` wrap into the next day; the
shipped default (1200 → 480) is the common path, not an edge case. `daysMask`
refers to the day the window *starts* (bit 0 = Monday … bit 6 = Sunday). Tests
cover: normal window, midnight-crossing window, exact boundary minutes 20:00:00
and 08:00:00, day-mask boundaries across the wrap, DST spring-forward and
fall-back inside a window, and the clock-moved-backwards guard (design §14).

- verify: `env JAVA_HOME=$HOME/.local/toolchains/jdk17 ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/.local/toolchains/android-sdk ./gradlew --no-daemon testDebugUnitTest --tests 'com.piercingxx.nopemode.core.ScheduleEvaluatorTest'`

### T2 — Override sealed interface + `NopeController.derive` truth table

`Override` sealed interface: `None`, `ForceOn(until: Instant?)`, `Break(until:
Instant)` — **`Break` has no unbounded variant, by construction** (design §6, D7).
`NopeController.derive(now, schedules, override)` implements the full §6 truth
table: `ForceOn` indefinite vs. expiring, `Break` auto-resume on expiry, and the
clock-moved-backwards guard (a `Break.until` in the future by more than max
duration cancels the break). Pure, no `android.*`.

- verify: `env JAVA_HOME=$HOME/.local/toolchains/jdk17 ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/.local/toolchains/android-sdk ./gradlew --no-daemon testDebugUnitTest --tests 'com.piercingxx.nopemode.core.NopeControllerTest'`

### T3 — BreakPolicy: minimum interval, budget, reset at window end

`BreakPolicy` enforces the anti-bypass rules (design §9): minimum interval
between breaks (default 30 min), break budget (default 3 per active window),
budget **reset at window end**, and all friction settings editable only while
inactive. Pure, no `android.*`. Tests cover interval enforcement, budget
exhaustion, and budget reset.

- verify: `env JAVA_HOME=$HOME/.local/toolchains/jdk17 ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/.local/toolchains/android-sdk ./gradlew --no-daemon testDebugUnitTest --tests 'com.piercingxx.nopemode.core.BreakPolicyTest'`
- files: `app/src/main/java/com/piercingxx/nopemode/core/BreakPolicy.kt`, `app/src/test/java/com/piercingxx/nopemode/core/BreakPolicyTest.kt`

### T4 — Next-boundary computation (WS6 pure slice)

`NextBoundary.next(now: LocalDateTime, schedules: List<Schedule>): LocalDateTime`
— the pure computation behind `AlarmScheduler`'s "next boundary only; recompute
and re-arm after each fire" rule (design §7.2). Given derived active state, the
next instant at which the active/inactive state flips. Pure, no `android.*`.
Tests cover a boundary inside the current window, the next-day wrap, and a
schedule that is currently inactive.

- verify: `env JAVA_HOME=$HOME/.local/toolchains/jdk17 ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/.local/toolchains/android-sdk ./gradlew --no-daemon testDebugUnitTest --tests 'com.piercingxx.nopemode.core.NextBoundaryTest'`

`SeedSchedule.defaultSchedule()` returns the `Schedule(1200, 480, all-days-mask,

`BackupJson` serializes and restores blocked apps, schedules, and settings as

## Deferred — operator on-device verification (no device/emulator here)

These are todo.md workstreams whose behavior **only a device can prove**. They
are NOT tasks in this marathon. Do not build them here; do not fake them with a
weaker check. Each item states WHAT the operator must verify on-device.

### WS2 — Room database wiring (DAOs, `NopeDatabase`, seed migration execution)
The five entities exist; the DAOs, `NopeDatabase`, and the seed `Migration`
object are missing. Room migrations and DAO behavior need an Android runtime and
are instrumented tests. **Verify on-device:** a fresh install has the 20:00→08:00
schedule with no user action; Room migration runs and the default row is present.

### WS5 — SuspendEnforcer
`setPackagesSuspended`, `suspend_record` crash safety (write record before
suspend), failure-array surfacing (R8), non-suspendable package exclusion at
selection time, active-IME hard-block + default-SMS explicit confirm, and boot
reconcile of orphans in `suspend_record`. **Verify on-device:** a blocked app
goes silent, greys out, and shows the system paused dialog; releasing restores
it fully. **Verify on SDK 37** (design §16). Never report success for a package
the platform refused to suspend.

### WS6 — Android scheduling parts (`AlarmScheduler`, `BootReceiver`)
`setExactAndAllowWhileIdle(RTC_WAKEUP)` next-boundary-only, re-arm after each
fire, exact-alarm degrade + persistent warning, `BOOT_COMPLETED`/`TIME_SET`/
`TIMEZONE_CHANGED`, and `reconcile()` on every trigger. The pure next-boundary
computation is T4 (buildable); the AlarmManager/BroadcastReceiver wiring is not.
**Verify on-device:** reboot at 02:00 inside the window → apps still suspended on
boot.

### WS7 — UI (five screens, `BlockedActivity`, break countdown notification)
Home (state, reason, master toggle, Take a break, blocked count, tier badge),
Blocked apps (searchable, non-suspendable shown disabled with inline reason),
Schedules (list/add/edit/delete, wrap shown explicitly), Settings (break
durations 5/15/30, min interval, budget — locked while active), Setup (tier,
provisioning command, fallback grants, relinquish + warning), `BlockedActivity`
interstitial, break countdown notification, AMOLED-black monochrome. **Verify
on-device:** every state in design §6 is reachable and legible from the UI.

### WS8 — Quick Settings tile
`NopeTileService : TileService` toggling `ForceOn`/clearing it, label + state
tracking derived state via `requestListeningState`. **Verify on-device:** the
tile reflects state changed from the app, and vice versa. Tile *placement* in
the shade stays a manual user step (`sysui_qs_tiles` is vestigial on Android 17).

### WS9 — FallbackEnforcer
`NopeNotificationListener` (cancel/snooze blocked packages while active),
`NopeAccessibilityService` (foreground detection → `BlockedActivity`), debounce
against launch loops, and UI stating plainly that this tier can let a sound
through and therefore does not satisfy R2. **Verify on-device:** with device
owner relinquished, blocks still work at the weaker tier.

### WS11 — Quiet Ringer (R9)
`RingerPolicy` creating the `AutomaticZenRule` once and persisting its id,
`ZenPolicy` with calls from **starred contacts only**, repeat-callers toggle
(built-in DND category), rule state driven by the same derived `isActive` inside
`reconcile()` (no second scheduler), `ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY` grant flow with
a loud Home warning when not granted, `removeAutomaticZenRule` on teardown, never
writing global DND state, and a one-time warning when the user has no starred
contacts. **Verify on-device:** with Nope-Mode active, a call from a non-starred
number does not ring; a starred contact does; toggling repeat callers changes
second-call behaviour; revoking DND access surfaces a visible warning. The zen
rule governs **the ringer only** — never app notifications generally (design
§18.1).

**T1 — ScheduleEvaluator: `shouldBeActiveAt` with midnight-crossing windows**

`ScheduleEvaluator.shouldBeActiveAt(now: LocalDateTime, schedules: List<Schedule>): Boolean` — pure, no `android.*`. Tests cover: normal window, midnight-crossing window, exact boundary minutes 20:00:00 and 08:00:00, day-mask boundaries across the wrap, DST spring-forward and fall-back inside a window.

Key semantics:
- A window is active on a given day if `daysMask` has the bit set for the day the window starts.
- For a normal window (`end > start`): active when `now.minuteOfDay` is in `[start, end)` on a day whose start-day bit is set.
- For a midnight-crossing window (`end <= start`): active when `now.minuteOfDay >= start` (on a start-day bit set) OR `now.minuteOfDay < end` (on the previous day's start bit set — i.e., the day the window wrapped into).

For exact boundaries: 20:00:00 is the start boundary (inclusive), 08:00:00 is the end boundary (exclusive). So the window is `[start, end)` for normal, and for wrap `[start, 1440) ∪ [0, end)`.

For the wrap case, the second segment `[0, end)` is active if the *previous* day's start bit was set (the day the window started).

DST: since we compare minute-of-day on local time, DST spring-forward/fall-back just works because LocalDateTime is wall-clock. The test constructs LocalDateTime values that cross DST boundaries and verifies the minute-of-day comparison is unaffected. Since we're using `LocalDateTime` (no zone), DST is inherently handled — the test just needs to exercise the logic with times around a DST transition to prove we don't do anything zone-dependent.

from datetime import datetime

# Mirror of ScheduleEvaluator.shouldBeActiveAt logic
def should_be_active_at(now, schedules):
    minute = now.hour * 60 + now.minute
    day_of_week = now.weekday()  # 0=Mon..6=Sun
    prev = (day_of_week + 6) % 7
    for s in schedules:
        if not s[4]:
            continue
        start, end, days_mask = s[1], s[2], s[3]
        def day_set(d):
            return (days_mask & (1 << d)) != 0
        if end > start:
            if start <= minute < end and day_set(day_of_week):
                return True
        else:
            if minute >= start and day_set(day_of_week):
                return True
            if minute < end and day_set(prev):
                return True
    return False

MON = 1<<0; TUE=1<<1; WED=1<<2; THU=1<<3; FRI=1<<4; SAT=1<<5; SUN=1<<6
ALL = MON|TUE|WED|THU|FRI|SAT|SUN
default = (1, 1200, 480, ALL, True)

def dt(y,m,d,h,mi): return datetime(y,m,d,h,mi)

fails = []
def check(desc, got, want):
    if got != want:
        fails.append((desc, got, want))

# normal window
s = (1, 540, 600, MON|TUE, True)
check("normal inside", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,10,9,30),[s]), True)
check("normal end excl", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,10,10,0),[s]), False)
check("normal before", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,10,8,59),[s]), False)
check("normal wrong day", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,12,9,30),[s]), False)

# midnight crossing
check("mc evening", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,10,21,0),[default]), True)
check("mc early", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,11,3,0),[default]), True)
check("mc midday", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,11,12,0),[default]), False)

# boundaries
check("start incl 20:00", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,10,20,0),[default]), True)
check("start-1min", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,10,19,59),[default]), False)
check("end-1min", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,11,7,59),[default]), True)
check("end excl 08:00", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,11,8,0),[default]), False)

check("mo 21:00", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,10,21,0),[monday_only]), True)
check("tue 03:00 wrap", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,11,3,0),[monday_only]), True)
check("tue 21:00", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,11,21,0),[monday_only]), False)
check("wed 03:00", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,12,3,0),[monday_only]), False)

check("mon 21:00", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,10,21,0),[sunday_only]), False)

check("dst spring 3:00", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,3,8,3,0),[default]), True)
check("dst spring 8:00", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,3,8,8,0),[default]), False)
check("dst fall 1:30", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,11,1,1,30),[default]), True)

# disabled / empty

check("disabled", should_be_active_at(dt(2026,8,10,21,0),[disabled]), False)

    15	 * Sunday). DST is handled implicitly: we compare minute-of-day on local wall
    16	 * clock time, so a spring-forward or fall-back inside a window changes the
    17	 * wall-clock duration but not the active/inactive decision (design §14).
    18	 */
    19	object ScheduleEvaluator {
    20	
    21	    /**

    23	     *
    24	     * A window is active on a given day when `daysMask` has the bit set for the
    25	     * day the window STARTS. For a normal window (`end > start`) that is the
    26	     * day [now] falls on. For a midnight-crossing window (`end <= start`) the
    27	     * wrap means the window also covers the early hours of the FOLLOWING day,
    28	     * which belong to the day whose start-day bit was set.
    29	     */
    30	    fun shouldBeActiveAt(now: LocalDateTime, schedules: List<Schedule>): Boolean {
    31	        val minute = now.hour * 60 + now.minute
    32	        val dayOfWeek = now.dayOfWeek.value - 1 // 0 = Monday .. 6 = Sunday
    33	        val previousDayOfWeek = (dayOfWeek + 6) % 7
    34	
    35	        for (schedule in schedules) {

    37	            val start = schedule.startMinuteOfDay
    38	            val end = schedule.endMinuteOfDay
    39	            if (end > start) {
    40	                // Normal window: [start, end) on the current day.
    41	                if (minute in start until end && isDaySet(schedule.daysMask, dayOfWeek)) {
    42	                    return true
    43	                }
    44	            } else {
    45	                // Midnight-crossing window: [start, 24:00) on the start day,
    46	                // plus [00:00, end) on the following day (which belongs to the
    47	                // day whose start-day bit was set).
    48	                if (minute >= start && isDaySet(schedule.daysMask, dayOfWeek)) {
    49	                    return true

    52	                    return true
